links.outcome: Validity of references cited by LLMs in PET/CT responses
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1: only 37% of cited references fully valid, 11.1% invalid. GPT-5.3: 33% fully valid, 7.4% invalid.
links.quote: only 37% of cited references were fully valid, with 11.1% being invalid.

links.outcome: Inter-trial consistency of regenerated LLM responses
links.effect: 7.7% of DeepSeek-R1 regenerated responses showed substantial inconsistencies, mainly tumor staging; GPT-5.3 5.1%; no significant difference (p = 1.00).
links.quote: However, 7.7% of regenerated responses showed substantial inconsistencies, primarily in tumor staging, and only 37% of cited references were fully valid, with 11.1% being invalid.

links.outcome: Primary and differential diagnosis accuracy on difficult PET/CT cases
links.effect: Both models reached 10% primary diagnosis accuracy and 60% differential diagnosis accuracy on 10 difficult cases.
links.quote: For the 10 identical difficult cases, both models reached 10% primary diagnosis accuracy and 60% differential diagnosis accuracy.

screen.reason: The study is an empirical evaluation comparing two generative LLMs (DeepSeek-R1 and GPT-5.3) on standardized PET/CT clinical tasks (FAQ answering, report interpretation, complex diagnostic reasoning) evaluated by expert physicians. It does not evaluate a deployment guardrail or practice.
